doc.title: Jim Galloway interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Establishing himself and balancing art with music
summary: He sat in, formed his own group after three years, and moved between art work and full-time music.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Just doing the union job. Wow. So how did you establish yourself as a player in Toronto?
I sat in with a lot of groups, then started getting calls for gigs. And three years after I’d been there I formed a little group of my own and gosh it’s been downhill from there.
How long did you keep up your art work?

Oh let’s see now, I guess I was on the road the first time full time in the late 60s. In the early 70s there was a bit of a nose dive for music, and I went back to my art background and was sort of combining that and playing, and then a couple of years, three years or so after that I went back into it full time and it’s been like that ever since.
